name: Company Wide AI Rollouts
blurb: How drugmakers moved generative AI from pilots to the whole workforce.
title: Company Wide AI Rollouts
answer: Several large drugmakers have put generative AI in front of most employees. Moderna deployed ChatGPT Enterprise with a goal of proficiency for every eligible employee and a network of internal champions, and Amgen scaled AI assistants across the company after measured testing and security review.

crumbs.name: AI Adoption and Governance in Life Sciences

reading.body:
Company wide generative AI rollouts in pharma succeeded when broad access came with training, use case guidance and internal champions, not access alone.

Two drugmakers show the pattern. Moderna put ChatGPT Enterprise in front of its workforce with a proficiency goal for every eligible employee and a network of internal champions. Amgen scaled AI assistants across the company after measured testing and security review. In both cases the deployment was company wide, and in both cases it was paired with something beyond the licence: a target, a support structure, or a review process.

The governance lesson is the useful part for AI specifically. A regulated company can move a general purpose model to most of its staff without abandoning oversight, provided the rollout carries training and guidance with it. The data covers two firms and two accounts, so it establishes that this path exists rather than that it is typical. It does not give adoption rates, cost, productivity results, or any comparison against companies that ran narrower pilots.

sections.body: Broad access works when it comes with training, use case guidance and champions; access alone produces little measurable change.
